I recently had to deal with Entra ID for the first time to setup Microsoft OAuth for our site and my god why is it so badly designed. Just creating a tenant is a PITA and you get a default tenant you can't change without paying for Microsoft 365.

You literally cannot change your tenant ID and the form by default picks a random one for you... Also by default you can't create a tenant without an existing Microsoft account, which everybody acknowledges is a chicken and egg problem.
It takes like two minutes to create a tenant. Click Next a bunch, enter a credit card, you're done.
after 36 years kerberos seems pretty stable, secure, and well supported finally. why do we need Entra?
New downgrade attack can bypass FIDO auth in Microsoft Entra ID. Pff.. again an Entra ID security flaw? It's incredible how sloppy their single auth solution is..

Most orgs will have TAP for account recovery... The attack sequence relies on the existence of an alternative authentication method besides FIDO, which tends to be the case with FIDO implementations since admins prefer to maintain a recovery option.

I've started enforcing users of privileged tools to go through a wireguard instance before being allowed to access Azure hosted tools that rely on Entra auth, as a mitigation for this browser-simulation downgrade attack.
Azure AD is simple and effective. What the heck is an Entra and why do I want it to manage my ids?

I work in a large Microsoft Shop that works with a lot of large enterprise customers. I doubt very much that anyone will start to say 'Entra ID' instead of Azure AD... This renaming is utterly pointless.
Maybe they could fix the naming scheme of Azure AD B2B and Azure AD B2C... Entra External ID and Entra External Verified ID... adding even more confusion plus future migration headaches.
Microsoft Entra ID Will Retire SMS and Voice Authentication. Passkeys really feel like a scheme to get us limited to a few blessed identity providers.

Microsoft Entra ID Remote Code Execution Vulnerability - CVE-2026-69836, CVSS 10.0, claimed no exploits. Since it was a fixed vuln in a closed-source cloud-based service, we will likely never have any more information.

Microsoft Entra ID Vulnerability Could Have Been Catastrophic. Companies feel secure using Microsoft's online offerings even after such vulnerabilities are shown; when MS has issues like this, people shrug and keep using them.
